title: Turning a container into display:flex blockifies its direct child — the new block box intercepts descendants' height:100% chains and collapses them to auto
trigger: After setting display:flex (column) on a shell element, a descendant that used height:100% (e.g. a video styled by the site to fill its player) collapses to content height — dead bands appear inside the shell even though the shell itself keeps its height
principle: Percentage heights resolve against the nearest ancestor with a definite height — and for in-flow elements, only block-level ancestors count; inline ancestors (framework host elements like Angular's <app-watch>) are skipped automatically. So do NOT give the shell display:flex to begin with: blockification is what creates the false containing block. Keep the shell's native display, give IT a definite height, then only pin width/height/min-height:100%/0 on intermediates — never their display (forcing display:block on a natively flex/grid intermediate explodes its children's arrangement, e.g. a horizontal control bar into a vertical icon column). Inline intermediates ignore the pinned height (harmless no-op) and are skipped by resolution anyway; block intermediates get re-linked; flex intermediates keep their layout mode. General rule: on host territory change metrics (width/height/inset/margin), never layout mode (display/position semantics).

cases.context: kisskh desktop: .col-12 shell (stretched to row height 736px) > APP-WATCH > MAT-VIDEO > .videoplayer{height:100%} > video. Natively .videoplayer skips the inline ancestors and takes .col-12's height → video fills the column. After split view set .col-12 to display:flex column, APP-WATCH blockified and .videoplayer collapsed 736→287 — video floated mid-stage with ~440px dead space. Separately, display:block!important on a flex/grid intermediate makes its children stack vertically — the broken-host-controls signature.

applyFor: Restructuring any element to display:flex/absolute when descendants rely on percentage heights
Debugging video/media that suddenly shrinks to natural height after a container became a flex context

check.command: Repro: Brave + kisskh desktop viewport — press 't'; the video element must fill the stage height (letterboxed content inside), not collapse to its natural 16:9 height.
